# Performance: pass-with-notes

Subject: pr:310. Round 2, final round. Exact head: 7f83e0defd62fb5da0170b02afb6af4872ccbaa3.

No new performance finding. The R310-F001 repair preserves the A1 cost reduction without a repeated zero-delay wake for an already-overdue row. Approval is source/CI proof, with deployed AFTER measurements still owed.

## Repair and no-spin check

The only new production work in the wait loop is one in-process `SystemTime::now()` per pass (`crates/daemon/src/delivery/mod.rs:2001-2007`). The timestamp is captured INSIDE the loop, before claiming, and passed to the existing next-due read at line 2288. It is not a request-lifetime cutoff.

`NEXT_CLAIMABLE_SQL` now selects `due > ?3`, with ?3 the pass-start epoch second (`crates/store/src/queue.rs:305-320,871-909`). A deadline crossed during that pass remains eligible and yields zero remaining duration, causing an immediate claim retry. The next pass captures a fresh cutoff at or after that crossed deadline, so that SAME overdue row is no longer selected, even if a running serial-key claim still prevents consumption. Due equality is excluded. The repair does not turn past-due rows into an unconditional zero-sleep poll.

An independent in-memory check executed the exact SQL extracted from this head: retained a crossed pending deadline, excluded overdue rows across 100 fresh cutoffs, retained a crossing lease deadline, excluded that lease at equality, and retained the jobs_claimable indexed kind/state search. This verifies the predicate; it is not a live daemon spin or CPU measurement.

## Cost rows remain valid

| Work | Cost after the repair |
|---|---|
| Undisturbed native idle request | Four passes at approximately 0/15/30/45 s; unchanged 55 s answer, no final deadline pass |
| 76 continuously waiting seats | Approximately 5.53 idle passes/s, versus 152/s before A1; PR's approximately 7/s remains conservative |
| Truly empty SQLite pass | Six existing statements plus schema PRAGMA and indexed next-due query: eight total; approximately 44 loop statements/s at 76 seats, versus 912/s before, excluding request admission |
| Crossed deadline | Immediate extra pass for that crossing, not repeated passes for the same old deadline |
| New process launches/sites | None |

Matching seat events, genuinely new timed work and nonempty queue transactions add work; these are not unconditional fleet ceilings. The indexed MIN still visits matching live pending/running rows, not constant work for arbitrarily large live backlogs. The repair adds a parameter binding, not another query or event subscription.

## Exact-head evidence

`just pr-freeze 310` returned FINAL at 7f83e0defd62fb5da0170b02afb6af4872ccbaa3 with all five CI checks passing. Successful Rust run 44871662403, job 136747316384, artifact 14693798372 selected from that job's upload log: all 15 focused regressions passed. These include the store crossing test, daemon claim-to-next-read crossing test (1.527 s), eight next-claimable store tests, six-recipient-read bound over 20 s, original wake/identity tests, and two-seat event isolation.

No local cargo build, mutation run, dependency installation, competing receiver, bounce or product edit. C25 boot reports node_modules absent; dependency-backed proof is exact-head CI, not a local TS pass.

`harness checks --quick --json` was attempted and exited 1: eight dependency/toolchain-backed sensors failed; Rust, route inventory and smoke were skipped. This is not a green local gate and does not replace the successful exact-head CI.

## AFTER proof I will take

Only after the prime's deployment, I will record the actual deployed commit/PID and allow at least one complete 55 s native request lifetime before sampling. I will take matched 60-120 s windows with `pij-rs --json ping` and `/bin/ps -p <observed-pid> -o time=,rss=,lstart=,comm=`, retaining both snapshots and monotonic elapsed time. I will report inbox completion/refusal deltas, active_us per completion and per second, daemon cumulative CPU delta as percent of one core, RSS, and reconciled exact per-site spawn deltas.

I will run `just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json` separately from CPU sampling because the machine sampler itself busy-polls. Fleet cohort, other route activity and event throughput will be recorded so a busier or quieter window is not mistaken for the feature's effect. Round-1 BEFORE was 64.927 ms/completion and 24.988% core on PID 22838/653f90ef96, with other fleet activity; its raw receipts remain the historical comparator, not a quiet-fleet guarantee. If intervening deployments or cohort changes make it unmatched, a fresh pre-bounce BEFORE window is needed for attribution.

The expected result is substantially lower empty-inbox active cost and lower matched daemon CPU, consistent with the approximately twentyfold empty-loop SQL reduction, with no new recurring launch cost. Exact timing ratios and CPU floor are not promised. Four idle passes/55 s and six recipient reads/20 s remain source/CI bounds unless live inner-pass instrumentation is available; ping completions are NOT pass counts.

Broadcast receive/filter cost remains W times total event rate and does not cause another seat's SQL pass. It still executes inside HeldSpan, so route active_us alone cannot prove its CPU cost. I will retain the event-rate/provenance limit when reporting residual CPU, rather than label fan-out dominant from wake counts alone.
